title: Readyroom: rapid rollback & rollout calendar (Apr 2028) - draft
checklist:
Preflight (T-48 to T-1)
- Validate canary config: 1% -> 5% over 30m -> 25% over 2h. Owner: Lina.
- Smoke tests: inference latency baseline, error-rate <0.5%, 95th p90 within SLO. Owner: Ethan.
- Telemetry hooks live: token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, KV cache miss rate. Owner: Priya.
- Backup model variants staged: v2-quant, v2-fp16, fallback v1.9. Repo tag: release/v2.0-rollback-ready.
- Database migrations: none. If any, run in separate maintenance window.
- Canary traffic routing rules and throttle policies preloaded into router (preview mode). Owner: Samir.
- Chatops runbook pinned to #release-ops and included in on-call pager. Confirmed.
- Communication: release email draft + status page template ready. Owner: Lina.
- Incident owners and escalation ladder confirmed (SRE, Serving Runtime, Product).

Day-Of (T-0 to +4h)
- T-0 (0900 PT): Kickoff in #release-ops – confirm all owners present and run quick preflight checklist. Note: T-0 can be delayed by max 15m.
- +00:05: Apply canary policy -> route 1% traffic to release lane. Watch telemetry for first 5 minutes.
- +00:30: If stable, step to 5% and run full smoke harness (end-to-end flows, auth, billing).
- +02:00: If stable and no regressions, step to 25% and open 90m observation window.
- +04:00: If stable, proceed to bulk rollout or follow scheduled stagger plan.

Rollback triggers (must be actionable)
- Sustained error rate >1% for 10 minutes on selected signal (inference errors, 5xx from runtime).
- Latency p95 increase >2x baseline for >5 minutes and not explained by load spike.
- Quality regression: webhook eval set shows BLEU/ROUGE drop beyond threshold OR critical prompt failure in curated set.
Action: run `release-ctrl rollback --to=release/v1.9` (ops-scripts), notify #release-ops, escalate to SRE lead.

Postmortem criteria
- Any rollback or SLO breach -> formal incident and 72h timeline for preliminary postmortem.
- Minor anomalies require annotated release note entry and follow-up ticket.

release_notes:
Draft release notes (internal -> public trim)
Title: Serving runtime v2.0 rollout (initial canary)
What’s new:
- Performance: Kernel selection improvements reduce per-token latency by ~12% median (internal bench).
- Cost: New batching heuristics reduce amortized GPU cycles for short sequences (~8% cost reduction for chat workloads).
- Reliability: KV cache persistence reduces cold-start misses on scaled pods.
- Ops: Canary-ready routing and automated rollback tooling (release-ctrl CLI).
Fixes included:
- Fix for stale KV eviction leading to hallucination in long-running conversations (REL-5112).
- Resolved an intermittent p95 spike when sequence length >1k (PR #318).
Known issues / caveats:
- Edge-case tokenization mismatch for a legacy customer prompt set (workaround: pin model to v1.9). Ticket: REL-5189.
- Quantized variant shows slightly higher perplexity on a small eval subset; not exposed in user-facing tests but flagged for follow-up evaluation.
Rollout plan summary:
- Canary -> regional ramp -> global: 48–72h expected to reach steady state unless manual hold/rollback required.
Post-release checks (T+24, T+72)
- T+24: Confirm error-rates, p95 latency, token cost delta, and top-10 prompts with highest divergence. Owner: Priya.
- T+72: Finalize rollout decision and close release checklist. Owner: Samir.
Unresolved / outstanding items
- Finalize SLO thresholds for new kernel paths (open action: assign owners for threshold tuning).
- Confirm billing calc change transparency for customers that use per-token metrics (finance + product review).
- Add synthetic prompts to eval set for the new quant variant.
body:
Summary: This readyroom document is a compact operational playbook for a fast-follow rollout where rollback needs to be immediate and low-friction. It combines a short, actionable preflight checklist, a tight T-0 -> T+4h calendar for canary progression, explicit rollback triggers with commands, and a draft of release notes and post-release checks.

Usage notes: keep one terminal open to run release-ctrl commands, one tab for Grafana/temporal traces, and the pinned Slack thread for status updates. If in doubt, default to rollback and escalate — aim to keep customer-facing impact to zero.

Appendix: Quick commands (ops-scripts repo)
- Start canary: `release-ctrl apply --policy canary-rapid --step=1`
- Promote step: `release-ctrl promote --to-step=2`
- Rollback: `release-ctrl rollback --to=release/v1.9 --reason=auto-trigger`
- Health snapshot: `telemetry-snapshot --tags=release,v2.0 --output=/tmp/release-YYYYMMDD.json`

If this doc becomes the runbook for a live rollout, convert to the canonical Confluence page and attach the final telemetry artifacts and postmortem link.
